summary: Researched RTX as one immutable aerospace and defence security, separating Collins, Pratt & Whitney, and Raytheon. Current results show defence and commercial demand converting into margins and cash, while engine liabilities, contract risk, cyclicality, and absent normalized valuation block a strategy. Updated the security to watching without follow-up work.

evidence.claim: RTX reported USD 24.7 billion sales, USD 289 billion backlog, USD 2.9 billion free cash flow, and margin expansion across all three segments.
Raytheon sales grew 18% on air-defence, naval, Patriot, Standard Missile, and AMRAAM volume; Pratt and Collins also grew with different margin and cycle exposures.

daily_report_items: RTX moved to watching: Raytheon, Pratt, and Collins converted demand into margin and cash growth, but engine, contract, cycle, and valuation gates block a strategy.
